results.title: ‘It a mash wi up’
results.description: AT least two Kingston entrepreneurs whose livelihoods depend on charging US Embassy visitors a fee to store their mobile devices or provide them with phone calls are requesting a meeting with embassy officials, seeking ways to adapt after a new policy permitting applicants to bring cellphones inside the facility. The applicants themselves have expressed mixed views about the policy change, with some welcoming the move, rejoicing that they no longer have to pay people outside the embassy to keep their devices while inside, and others expressing scepticism. Cellphones are just one of the many items now permitted within the walls of the US Embassy. In an advisory on September 1 the embassy said small quantities of baby formula, baby food, milk, diapers, and baby carriers that can pass through an X-ray machine are now permitted. Other items include money, belts, watches, keys, earbuds, medical devices, and non-liquid medication, which must be declared before security screening. Prohibited items include computers, intelligent eyewear, and other electronic devices, inclusive of media devices, such as compact discs (CDs), thumb drives, memory cards, flash drives, headphones, and speakers. Additionally, cameras or video equipment, flashlights, lighters and matches, weapons, knives, and other sharp objects are not allowed. Alcoholic beverages, purses larger than 18 inches, liquids, lotions, oils, and gels are also not allowed inside. But for Nicole Watson, a vendor who, for more than 15 years, has made a living holding on to cellphones for visa applicants, the move to allow previously banned cellphones is most troubling. “It’s something that we all live off [of]. I don’t know what transpired; it’s odd. We are out here to help each and every one. You have good, and you have bad, but we would just like the embassy to look over things or draw us in a meeting because this is our daily bread. If there are bad apples out here that they need to talk to, they can talk to them to keep the things flowing because we have kids to go to school,” she told the Jamaica Observer , lamenting the cost of living. Watson said the change has destroyed her business. “It a mash we up; it crush up, it gone,” she bemoaned. “I normally have around four buses that come to me in the morning time from May Pen, Mandeville, Savanna-la-Mar, and Montego Bay. I reach here like five in the morning time, or if them call me four o’clock, I will reach down. If possible, I would get 30 people for the day, because I’m known down here, so people just come... On a good day, about 500 or 600 persons come to them [at the embassy], so I can get at least 35 people. Now, everybody passes,” she said. Watson shared that she typically charges $1,000 to store cellphones, $300 for phone calls, and $500 for WhatsApp phone calls, money she said added up to support her and her children, but now she is barely making ends meet. “It’s hard because the sun is hot and business is slow,” she said. A look around the area outside the embassy proved her words to be true, as many other runners sat in the sun along the side of the road across from the embassy, eagerly awaiting business that never came. Watson had just two phones in her bag; she said she got them from loyal customers who still support her business. “Because I am out here long time, I will have my clients who come and I will say, ‘Alright, just give me a lunch money and gwaan,’ but from people hear what is going on now they just move along. We nuh bother press anybody; we just make them move along,” she told the Sunday Observer . Despite slow business, Watson said she will not leave the area. Instead, she will continue to sell phone cards and beverages. “Food have to eat, and gas have to buy. Me nah go do no nine-to-five work because me nah work for $17,000 a week. I cyaan bother with that because that can’t buy gas put in car,” she reasoned. Another vendor, who chose to remain anonymous, expressed concern that she would not be able to take care of her children. “My son inna 10 grade and my daughter inna eight grade, and it’s this send them go [to] school... I start it from them in basic school, then primary school, and now high school... I don’t know how me a go manage,” she said. “A me alone a take care of them, no father, no nothing. Me nuh have no help,” she bemoaned. “It mash up. If we can talk to them and bring it back, that would be good, but I don’t think talking a go bring it back either. We just have to have in our mind what else we are going to do after,” she said. Outside the embassy, applicants and family members sat patiently, awaiting their appointment. For some, the move to allow cellphones was welcomed, but one man was sceptical. “When I came here last week and I heard about it, I told the person, ‘Don’t take your phone inside there’, ” he said, adding that he planned to leave his phone in his car. However, for a woman who gave her name as Jennifer, she loved the idea of not having to stress about where she would store her cellphone. “The first time I came here I had to pay somebody to keep my phone outside, so it’s a good idea. At the time, I did not know that I could not bring in lotion and stuff in my bag, so when I got here I had to throw away things, so it’s good. At least we don’t have to pay money out here now because sometimes they charge $1,500 to hold the phone, and that can buy credit. It’s a good move,” she told the Sunday Observer .

results.title: Contact lost with Indonesia ferry carrying 243 in bad weather: rescue agency
results.description:
Jakarta: An Indonesian ferry carrying 243 passengers and crew is out of contact while sailing north in bad weather from Java to Borneo, rescue officials said Sunday.

The passenger and cargo ship Virgo Transport 8 departed from Surabaya, East Java, on Saturday before running into bad weather and losing contact with its shipping company early on Sunday.

"We have received the report regarding the loss of contact with the Virgo Transport 8 vessel and have immediately deployed personnel and KN SAR Laksmana 241 to the estimated last known position," said I Putu Sudayana, head of the Banjarmasin Search and Rescue Office.

"Considering the relatively large number of passengers and crew on board, we are optimising coordination with all relevant elements to accelerate the search process and ensure the safety of all passengers and crew."

Search and rescue operations were launched on Sunday morning, involving the navy, police and shipping company, Virgo.

The vessel's last position was detected in the waters of the Java Sea, around 150 kilometres (90 miles) from its destination, Banjarmasin pier, Sudayana said.

Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia -- an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that relies heavily on boat connections for daily transport and tourism.

Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.

On Monday, a speedboat carrying eight people, including five journalists working for local and international news agencies went missing near a volcano, Mount Anak Krakatau, in Banten province and a search is ongoing.

The journalists were sent to cover the volcano's eruption that paralysed Jakarta's main airport and several others.

Last month, a fire on board a ferry killed one person and left five others missing while 211 were rescued in the Lombok Strait off Indonesia's Bali island.

The ferry had been heading from Bali to Lombok when it ran into trouble in the early hours of August 12.

In July, a ferry transporting more than 70 people sank while sailing near Selayar, a small island south of Sulawesi.

results.title: MLS: Messi scores but Inter Miami playout 2-2 draw against Nashville
results.description: Miami, September 13 (IANS) A goal from captain Lionel Messi, who has now recorded 99 goals across all competitions for Inter Miami, and an own goal secured the point for the Inter Miami with a 2-2 draw at home against Nashville SC in MLS regular season action at the Nu Stadium.The visitors opened the scoring in the 4th minute to take the lead through a goal from Sam Surridge. Inter Miami equalised in the 19th minute through an own goal, as a corner kick delivery from Messi was deflected into the back of the net by Nashville defender Reed Baker-Whiting.The 1-1 scoreline then remained unchanged through the end of the first half.Inter Miami had a clear chance to take the lead early in the second half in the 50th minute, but Messi’s left-footed hit from the right side of the box rattled the crossbar.Twelve minutes later Messi made no mistake as Inter Miami turned the scoring around to take a 2-1 lead in the 62nd minute. Messi received a pass from De Paul in a central position just outside the box, where he unleashed a first-time, left-footed hit to find the back of the net at the far post as he recorded his 19th goal this regular season to take the lead in the race for the MLS Golden Boot, while at the same time reaching 99 strikes for Inter Miami across all competitions since joining the Club in 2023.The 66th minute of play saw Inter Miami make two substitutions, including the introduction of recently signed Paraguayan international midfielder Matías Galarza in place of Segovia as he made his debut for our Club.Inter Miami nearly extended its advantage through a double opportunity in the 78th minute. An initial shot from Suárez from the center of the box was met by a save by Nashville SC goalkeeper Brian Schwake, followed by an effort from Messi that was deflected by the visitor’s goalkeeper before bouncing off the left post.Nashville tied the match in the first minute of stoppage time through a goal from Surridge.Inter Miami pushed in search of reclaiming its lead and came close to finding a winner in the fourth minute of added time when a finish from De Paul from the right side of the box hit the left post.The 2-2 scoreline ultimately remained unchanged as Inter Miami secured a point tonight at Nu Stadium.

results.title: Search underway for Indonesian passenger ship carrying more than 240 people after it loses contact
results.description: Indonesian rescuers have launched a search operation after a passenger ship carrying more than 240 people lost contact in the Java Sea while traveling from East Java to South Kalimantan on Borneo island. The Search and Rescue Office in Banjarmasin, a city in South Kalimantan province, said they received a report the Virgo Transport 8 had experienced a communication failure while en route to the city from Surabaya, Indonesia’s second largest city in East Java province. Initial information indicated the vessel’s last known position was in the Java Sea, about 92 miles from a pier in Banjarmasin. There were no immediate reports of casualties.
